en: Yesterday I read a tablet.

distractors: Crās tabulam lēgī.
_crās_ means “tomorrow”, but _lēgī_ is in the perfect tense (it already happened). For yesterday: _herī_.
Herī tabulā lēgī.
_tabulā_ is ablative singular, but it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative: _tabulam_.
Herī tabulam lēgistis.
_lēgistis_ is 2nd person plural (perfect tense) of _legō_ (“you all read”). That would say “Yesterday you all read a tablet” instead of “Yesterday I read a tablet”.
